items.stem: What should drive the structure of a persuasive presentation?

options.text: A single core message and audience need
options.rationale: Correct: a clear message and audience drive what to include and the order.
Slide count is a container, not the driver of structure.
Templates style the deck but do not define the argument.

options.text: How much the presenter can read aloud
options.rationale: Delivery length follows from the message, not vice versa.

items.explanation: Correct: a clear message and audience drive what to include and the order.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: A slide contains the entire spoken script. What is the best fix?

options.text: Move detail to speaker notes and keep a headline plus key points
options.rationale: Correct: slides should support the talk with concise points while detail lives in notes.

options.text: Shrink the font so it all fits
options.rationale: Smaller text keeps the overload problem and hurts readability.

options.text: Add more slides with the same text
options.rationale: Duplicating text does not solve overload.
Reading dense slides disengages the audience.

items.explanation: Correct: slides should support the talk with concise points while detail lives in notes.

items.stem: Which TWO improve a data slide's honesty? (Select TWO)

options.text: Use axis scales that do not exaggerate differences
options.rationale: Correct: truthful scales prevent misleading the audience.

options.text: Label the source and time period
options.rationale: Correct: provenance lets the audience judge the data.

options.text: Truncate the axis to dramatise a small change
options.rationale: Truncation to dramatise is a misleading practice.
Removing the legend can make the chart unreadable or ambiguous.

items.explanation: Correct: truthful scales prevent misleading the audience.
